query: How does gravity scale with mass?
generated_response: Gravity scales with the square of the mass. This means that if you double the mass of an object, its gravitational pull will increase by four times. For example, if a planet has twice the mass of Earth, it would have four times the gravitational force. This is why the Moon orbits the Earth at a distance that is only about 1/6th of the distance between Earth and the Sun.
